messages.author: 61ec521265480c25
messages.subject: Secure password handling
parts:
I have developed a first prototype for handling passwords in a secure way, and would like to ask anybody with interest in the topic to provide some feedback to it. I put it into the gist at https://gist.github.com/ojessen/8656652 

The beef is in the following function:

# I'm following the recommendations in
# https://crackstation.net/hashing-security.htm
salt = paste0(runif(1, max = 1e9),runif(1, max = 1e9))
hash = digest(paste0(salt,input$loginRegister), algo="sha256")
# userTable as standin for the table in the database.
# The aim is to avoid having to
# login_clear obviously is for testing the behaviour,
# and not supposed to be in a real app.
if(!exists("userTable", envir=.GlobalEnv)){
userTable <<- data.frame(user = input$userNameRegister,
login =hash,
login_clear = input$loginRegister,
nacl = salt)

messages.author: bbc57ffa8a14ad13
messages.subject: Re: Secure password handling
parts:
Looks neat!  You could also consider using rscrypt which provides scrypt hashing instead of just sha256 and may simplify some of your logic with maintaining a separate salt.

But I think this is a neat model for those who want to securely store user credentials in Shiny (as long as their applications are using HTTPS).

Jeff

messages.author: 5589cace60501004
messages.subject: Re: Secure password handling
parts:
You can use a shiny-server together with a nginx webserver. The nginx webserver can be used with ssl (see: http://stackoverflow.com/questions/19934190/shiny-server-on-nginx-with-ssl) such that the connection cannot be sniffed. 

I build a simple login example with a ssl-connection on my webserver (github: https://github.com/sipemu/Shiny_Login): https://185.21.100.236:3636/ODM/ (demo/demo).

messages.author: bbc57ffa8a14ad13
messages.subject: Re: Secure password handling
parts:
It would be nice to see a tutorial on nginx + Shiny Server. Hopefully we or someone in the community can devote some time to getting that together.

As Michael mentioned, the official solution to the problem is Shiny Server Pro, which has built-in support for SSL (example) and user-authentication. It also does the password hashing for you (using scrypt) if you use the Flat-File authentication system (LDAP and Active Directory are also available, if you're in an organization that uses those).

Jeff
